As I have said in a previous thread, I'm just getting back into the game after a long break, but when I was an active and competitive player, I transferred around a little bit. I found that there were some major perks to both low pop and high pop servers.

Low population servers are infinitely better to do hunts on. There's way less chance of some jerk pulling early, because they actually NEED to wait for everyone to show up to kill the monster, and because the server is small enough that the handful of hunt linkshells running are all in communication with each other, so if you're that jerk more than a few times everybody learns your name and you don't get invited to parties any longer. People working on spawning some of the S ranks coordinate it with everyone, and there just seems to be a tighter knit community on a small server, so there's less douchebaggery.

That said, the larger population servers are way easier to find parties on. If you want to farm old content for mounts, are behind in the quest lines related to primals, or trying to grind older dungeons for levels, you're going to find it in party finder, or fill a group quickly if you start one. On a smaller population server you're much more dependent on your FC to help you catch up if you fall behind, and you will spend more time doing things YOU don't need so that other people will later help YOU with things YOU need. I'm not sure that's a bad thing, but it's definitely inconvenient at times.

I'm curious with the new overflow system on the zones if there are other new problems / benefits arising from high / low population servers. What's everyone else's experience?
Low population vs high population servers : your preference / opinion?

In those days I preferred being on low population server, it felt more like a brave new world with a few scrappy adventurers. However when my guild started to fall apart post 2.3 I realized I did not enjoy the low-pop environment as much when I was playing alone. It became difficult to find groups, or even just socialize in general.

I had a hard time finding an FC that had any more than 5 people on at a time. Being a bit of a social butterfly the lack of group activities and communication was killing my love of the game. I've since transferred to a higher pop server and have been enjoying myself much more.

It all comes down to personal preference. I've learned I like having a medium-large friendly group you can rely on, and who can rely on you.
